scope: Current official New Zealand sources required by the governing audit prompt. Source facts, audit inferences, and specialist decisions are deliberately separated.

sources.title: Health Information Privacy Code 2020
sources.current_marker: The official page identifies the consolidated code in force from 1 May 2026 and Amendment No 2 made in March 2026.
source_facts: The Code covers identifiable health information collected, used, held, and disclosed by health agencies.
The official applicability examples include supported accommodation and disability services.
Amendment No 2 reflects IPP3A and is in force from 1 May 2026 for indirect collection obligations.
sources.audit_inference: Oblivion workflows that receive health information from providers, integrations, delegates, devices, or imported records need explicit provenance and a reviewable decision about any required indirect-collection notice. This source does not by itself specify the product implementation or prove compliance.
sources.specialist_decision_required: A New Zealand privacy officer or lawyer must confirm which Oblivion collection pathways trigger the amended Code, applicable exceptions, notice content, timing, and records of the decision.

sources.title: HISO 10029:2022 Health Information Security Framework
sources.authority: Health Information Standards Organisation, Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora
sources.current_marker: The official PDF title and asset were indexed on the current Health New Zealand domain; the audit fetch could not retrieve the full PDF and therefore does not claim a complete control mapping.
source_facts: The current official asset is identified as HISO 10029:2022 Health Information Security Framework.
The indexed official excerpt describes Māori co-design and Te Tiriti-based stewardship goals.
The full framework content was not directly retrieved in this lane.
sources.audit_inference: Security, privacy, data stewardship, access control, incident, supplier, and resilience findings should eventually be mapped to the full framework, but the blocked fetch prevents Pass 6 completion credit.
sources.specialist_decision_required: A qualified health-information security owner must supply or review the authoritative framework and decide applicability, control ownership, evidence, and residual risk.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR New Zealand Base Implementation Guide
sources.authority: HL7 New Zealand; reached from the Health New Zealand NZ FHIR Registry link
sources.current_marker: Version 3.1.0, release, active as of 24 July 2026, based on FHIR R4.
source_facts: The guide provides reusable New Zealand extensions, identifiers, terminology, naming systems, and profiles.
It prefers reuse of suitable core, international, or recognised-registry definitions.
The guide explicitly does not define complete conformance requirements for a particular implementation or use case.
sources.audit_inference: Oblivion interfaces using FHIR should reuse current NZ identifiers and terminology where applicable, while each interface still needs a use-case-specific implementation guide or conformance contract.
sources.specialist_decision_required: An interoperability architect and clinical data owner must determine applicable profiles, interactions, terminology bindings, identifier rules, versioning, and validation evidence for each interface.

sources.title: Ngā Paerewa Health and Disability Services Standard NZS 8134:2021
sources.current_marker: The Ministry page says NZS 8134:2021 remains in effect and was under review; page last-updated marker 11 February 2026.
source_facts: NZS 8134:2021 has been in effect since 28 February 2022.
The standard is applicable to disability services and suitable for home and community support services.
The official summary describes person- and whānau-centred outcomes, cultural safety, equity, responsiveness to Māori, and a modular certification framework.
sources.audit_inference: Oblivion evidence and workflows should support person and whānau agency, culturally safe communication, outcome evidence, and module-appropriate assurance; source inspection cannot establish certification.
sources.specialist_decision_required: A qualified service quality lead or designated auditing agency must determine the exact applicable criteria and assess operational evidence; the ongoing standards review should be monitored.

sources.title: Code of Health and Disability Services Consumers' Rights
sources.current_marker: The official HDC page sets out the current Code and provider duties.
source_facts: The Code includes privacy and culturally responsive treatment, dignity and independence, appropriate standards, harm minimisation, and continuity between providers.
It requires effective communication and information a reasonable consumer needs for informed choice and consent.
It preserves competence to the appropriate extent, the right to refuse or withdraw consent, support-person rights, and a fair, simple, speedy, and efficient complaints process.
sources.audit_inference: Client, consent, clinical, medication, complaints, portal, delegate, and communication workflows need observable support for understandable information, agency, refusal/withdrawal, privacy, continuity, and complaint progression. The Code does not dictate a particular UI.
sources.specialist_decision_required: A clinical governance and consumer-rights specialist must validate how each workflow evidences these rights, including exceptions and supported decision-making.

sources.title: Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 overview
sources.current_marker: WorkSafe's page was updated 13 July 2026 and records amendments passed but not coming into force until 1 April 2027.
source_facts: HSWA is the current New Zealand workplace health and safety law as at the audit date.
The official overview emphasises participation, leadership, accountability, proactive risk management, primary business responsibility, officer due diligence, and worker duties.
The official page says passed amendments take effect on 1 April 2027, after this audit date.
sources.audit_inference: Oblivion H&S workflows should make hazards, risk ownership, worker participation, actions, evidence, escalation, and assurance reviewable; event logging alone is not sufficient. The audit must not prematurely apply the 2027 changes as current law.
sources.specialist_decision_required: A PCBU health-and-safety lead and New Zealand legal adviser must confirm the duties, record requirements, sector guidance, and readiness work for the 2027 amendments.

cross_source_rules: Do not convert an official source fact into a product compliance claim without application evidence and a qualified applicability decision.
Record future-effective changes separately from law and standards in force at the audit date.

Preserve the single-tenant, multi-Site architecture; privacy and safety scope is expressed through exact action authority, approved Site access, canonical ownership, direct-object concealment, and minimum-necessary disclosure.
No source in this register authorises remediation or proves clinical, legal, security, certification, interoperability, or release readiness.
